title: Speed Limit for Information Acquisition in Stochastic Learning Dynamics
abstract: Neural networks acquire internal representations through learning. In this work, we formulate stochastic gradient descent (SGD) as a Markovian stochastic process and derive a Fisher-information flow speed limit that bounds the rate at which trainable parameters can acquire information about latent variables in the data-generating process. The resulting inequality decomposes the information flow into drift and noise contributions, thereby quantifying the roles of deterministic learning forces and SGD-induced fluctuations from an information-theoretic perspective. We verify the bound in analytically tractable basis-function linear regression, where the information budget predicted by the bound reproduces the ordering and characteristic time scales with which different latent variables are encoded in the learned parameters. These results establish Fisher-information speed limits as a quantitative framework for diagnosing when and how different aspects of the data-generating mechanism are acquired during stochastic learning.
summary: This work establishes a Fisher-information speed limit that quantifies the maximum rate at which a neural network can learn about underlying latent variables during stochastic training. By modeling SGD as a stochastic process, the authors decompose this rate into deterministic (drift) and fluctuating (noise) components. This provides a powerful, information-theoretic diagnostic tool for understanding the efficiency and limits of machine learning algorithms.
main_problem: To derive a Fisher-information flow speed limit that bounds the rate at which trainable parameters in neural networks acquire information about latent variables during stochastic learning.
main_result: The rate of information acquisition is bounded by the sum of drift and noise contributions, and this bound is shown to be tight at the peak of the flow in analytically tractable models.
method: The authors formulate Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) as a Markovian stochastic process and utilize the Fisher information framework to derive an upper bound on the information flow.
model_or_system: The model is stochastic learning dynamics, specifically analyzing SGD applied to supervised learning where data is generated from a latent variable $Z$. The analysis is specialized to basis-function linear regression, whose dynamics near convergence reduce to an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process.
key_observables: Fisher-information flow ($J_{	heta, \chi}^{Z,t}$), Fisher information ($F_{	heta}^{Z,t}$), Drift information budget ($I_{	ext{drift}, \chi}^{Z,t}$), and Noise information budget ($I_{	ext{noise}, \chi}^{Z,t}$).
important_parameters: Relaxation rates ($\lambda_i$), characteristic time scales ($	au_{\chi, i}$), and the ratio of initial to final covariance values.
main_assumptions: The mini-batch fluctuation is approximated as Gaussian, and the analysis relies on deriving an upper bound, which is not necessarily an exact decomposition of the actual flow.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of Fisher information and the instantaneous flow, comparing the measured flow against the theoretical speed limit derived from the drift and noise components, showing the bound is tight at the peak.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general Fisher-information flow speed limit for SGD, then specializes this framework to linear regression. It analyzes the dynamics using modal decomposition, showing that the peak time of the information flow matches the relaxation time of the drift budget for each mode.
why_interesting: The use of information-theoretic speed limits to characterize the dynamics of complex, non-equilibrium learning processes provides a quantitative physical analogy to relaxation dynamics seen in many-body systems or open quantum systems.
